tutorial.title: Intro to SQLite
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to set up a SQLite database and query it

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent: Let's connect what we've learned about databases and backends so far. Now, we'll start working with a SQLite database within Node.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent: We use an NPM package called better-sqlite3 to help us interact with our database.

lessons.title: Lesson #3 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
First, we need to import it into our application using the require function.

Make sure to pick require, followed by "better-sqlite3".

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
Next, we'll store the imported module in a variable Database, allowing us to interact with the SQLite database throughout our application.

Make sure to pick Database.

lessons.title: Lesson #4 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
The next step is to initiate the database by creating a new instance of a SQLite database.

We create a new instance with the keyword new followed by the name of our variable. We also specify the name of the database file.

Make sure to pick new, followed by Database, and finally "./database.db".

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
We define the location of the database file when creating a new one. ./ refers to the current directory.

This code will either load an existing database from the specified location or create a new one if it doesn't already exist.

Make sure to pick ., followed by /.

lessons.title: Lesson #4 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We also store the new instance of the SQLite database in a new variable for easy access later.

Make sure to pick const, followed by db, and finally =.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Store the instance in db and prevent reassignment of that variable.

Make sure to pick const, followed by db, and finally =.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
Now it's time to put everything to work! With db.exec we can run SQL statements such as creating tables or inserting data.

It doesn't return anything, though. But we don't need that when we want to create a new table.

Make sure to pick db, followed by .exec.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Use db.exec to run SQL statements such as creating tables or inserting data without returning result rows.

Use the database instance to execute the SQL command that creates the pets table without returning rows.

Make sure to pick db, followed by .exec, CREATE, and finally TABLE.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
Use the exec method again to recreate the database you see here.

Make sure to pick db, followed by .exec.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Using db.exec, you can also add multiple values.

Make sure to type db.exec.

lessons.title: Lesson #4 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Require better-sqlite3.

Make sure to pick require followed by ( and then "better-sqlite3", ).
lessons.hardModeContent:
Load the better-sqlite3 package before creating the database instance.

Make sure to pick require, followed by (, "better-sqlite3", and finally ).

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the purpose of db.exec?

It executes a SQL command, such as creating tables or inserting data, without returning any resultIt retrieves data from the database and returns the result

It executes a SQL command, such as creating tables or inserting data, without returning any result.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Which database task should use db.exec because no result rows are needed?

Creating a table or inserting data without returning a result.Retrieving rows from a query.Opening an existing database file.

Creating a table or inserting data without returning a result.

lessons.title: Lesson #4 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Create a new database called database.

Make sure to pick "./database.db".
lessons.hardModeContent:
Create the database file named database.db in the current directory.

Make sure to pick "./database.db".

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does require("better-sqlite3") do?

It imports the better-sqlite3 module for SQLite database operationsIt opens an existing SQLite database file

It imports the better-sqlite3 module for SQLite database operations.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Before a program can create a SQLite database, what does require("better-sqlite3") provide?

The SQLite module for database operations.An already-open SQLite database file.A SQL query result.

The SQLite module for database operations.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Complete the code so we create a new database and add a first value.

Make sure to pick db followed by . and then exec, db, ., exec.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Run both database setup statements: first create the pets table, then add Tom.

Make sure to pick db, followed by ., exec, db, ., and finally exec.

lessons.title: Lesson #4 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We'll now look at queries that return data, such as selecting data from a table.

When querying a database, we use the prepare method. This sets up the SQL statement so it can be executed later.

Make sure to pick db, followed by .prepare.

lessons.title: Lesson #4 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We pass the SQL query as a string as an argument to the prepare method.

Create a SELECT query and provide it as the argument.

Make sure to pick SELECT followed by * and then FROM, users.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Pass the SQL query as a string argument to the prepare method.

Prepare a query that selects every column from users.

Make sure to pick SELECT, followed by *, FROM, and finally users.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can save the prepared query in a variable.

Make sure to pick const, followed by getUsersQuery.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can save the prepared query in a variable.

Store the prepared query in getUsersQuery and prevent reassignment.

Make sure to pick const, followed by getUsersQuery, =, db, and finally prepare.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
To run the query, call the all method on the prepared statement.

Make sure to pick getUsersQuery, followed by .all().
lessons.hardModeContent:
To run the query, call the all method on the prepared statement.

Run the prepared query, save every returned row in users, then log it.

Make sure to pick users, followed by getUsersQuery, all, and finally users.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
The get method is used to retrieve a single row from the result set.

Make sure to pick get.
lessons.hardModeContent:
The get method is used to retrieve a single row from the result set.

Run the prepared statement, save its one returned row in user, then log it.

Make sure to pick user, followed by getUserByIdQuery, get, and finally user.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
We can also prepare a SELECT statement with parameters using question marks ?. For example, to select a user by their id.

If we pass a value when executing the query, it will replace the question mark, allowing us to filter the results dynamically.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by 50.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You can prepare a SELECT statement with ? parameters, for example to select a user by id.

Pass a value when executing the query to replace the question mark and filter the results dynamically.

Use 50 for the parameter and retrieve a single row as an object.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by user, get, and finally 50.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
If we try to get an entry that doesn't exist, we receive undefined.

Try to query a user with the id 500 that will not return a value.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by 500.
lessons.hardModeContent:
If you try to get an entry that does not exist, you receive undefined.

Retrieve a single row with the missing id 500, then log the result.

Make sure to pick ?, followed by user, get, and finally 500.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the get method do?

It retrieves a single row from the result setIt retrieves all rows from the result set

It retrieves a single row from the result set.
lessons.hardModeContent:
You need one matching user, not an array of results. Which method should you call on the prepared statement?

getallprepare

Make sure to pick get.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the purpose of the question mark ? in a prepared SQL query?

It acts as a placeholder for values that are passed when the query is executedIt indicates that the query is optional

It acts as a placeholder for values that are passed when the query is executed.
lessons.hardModeContent:
A prepared query contains WHERE id = ?, then runs with get(50). What does ? stand for?

The value passed to get when the query runs.A table name that must be chosen first.A sign that the whole query is optional.

The value passed to get when the query runs.

lessons.title: Lesson #5 - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Prepare a query and execute it to get all entries from the pets table.

Make sure to pick getPetsQuery followed by db and then ., prepare, getPetsQuery, .all().
lessons.hardModeContent:
Prepare a query that selects every column from pets, then run it and log every returned row.

Make sure to pick getPetsQuery, followed by db, prepare, SELECT, *, FROM, pets, pets, getPetsQuery, and finally all.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does the all method return?

It returns an array of all rows from the result setIt returns only the first row from the result set

It returns an array of all rows from the result set.
lessons.hardModeContent:
After a prepared query runs with all, what is stored in its result variable?

An array containing every returned row.Only the first returned row.The SQL query as a string.

An array containing every returned row.

lessons.title: Lesson #6 - Copy - Copy
lessons.interactiveContent:
Prepare a dynamic SELECT statement.

Make sure to pick WHERE followed by id and then =, ?.
lessons.hardModeContent:
Prepare a dynamic SELECT statement.

Select the pet whose id is supplied as 50, then log that one row.

Make sure to pick getUserByIdQuery, followed by =, db, prepare, WHERE, id, ?, getUserByIdQuery, get, 50, and finally user.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
What does db.prepare do here?

It prepares a SQL query for execution It executes a prepared SQL query

It prepares a SQL query for execution.
lessons.hardModeContent:
In this prepared query, what is the ? for when the statement is executed later?

It receives the id value used to filter the rows.It names the table to query.It runs the query immediately.

It receives the id value used to filter the rows.
